title: Breaking Up Is Hard To Do
text:
Breaking Up Is Hard To Do

Tom Hancock, AJ Cortese

Gavekal Technologies: Briefing | 21 Sep 2026

Both China and the US have devoted intense energy to slashing their technological reliance on each other. These efforts have had some impact, but the overall lesson is that decoupling is really difficult. The list of sectors with entrenched (and often two-way) dependencies includes biotech, robots, semiconductors, optical transceivers, medical devices, lidar sensors, solar inverters, gas turbines, batteries and electricity grid equipment. And even as old dependencies are cut, new ones pop up. The underlying causes are the powerful complementarity of American demand and innovation with Chinese manufacturing efficiency and scale, the persistence of talent flows, and China’s technological progress—which makes its high-end tech companies more dependent on specialized US inputs.Also in this issue of China Tech Brief:
